# Tracery

> Generative geometric marks — minimal compositions of circles, polygons and
> lines, driven by a seed so any mark is reproducible. Free, no key, no install.
> https://pierrelouislabonne.github.io/tracery/

## Read this first

**The page renders client-side, into a `<canvas>`. Fetching the URL returns an
empty shell — there is no mark in the HTTP response, and no server-side render.**
You need a real browser (Playwright, Puppeteer, a browser-automation tool). If
all you can do is fetch URLs, you cannot use Tracery.

What not to do — each of these costs you dearly, and none of them is necessary:

- **Do not read `index.html`.** Everything you need is on this page. The source
  is 45 KB of geometry you will never call directly.
- **Do not screenshot the page.** The deliverable is the string returned by
  `toSVG()`, written straight to a file. You never have to *see* the mark to
  produce it. Take a screenshot only if you must judge the result visually —
  choosing between candidates, say — and never as a way of checking that the
  export worked.
- **Do not recreate the mark.** Never redraw it from a screenshot, and never
  hand-write SVG that imitates it. The only valid output is the exact string
  `toSVG()` returned — anything else has different geometry, and its `url` no
  longer reproduces it.

The whole job is one script (below), one process, one file written.

## Recipe

Run this and you are done — no page inspection, no screenshot, no second pass:

```js
// node get-mark.js  ·  npm i playwright
const { chromium } = require('playwright');
const fs = require('fs');

const url = 'https://pierrelouislabonne.github.io/tracery/'
          + '?seed=8421&rule=orbit&dark=0&grid=0';

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const page = await browser.newPage();
  await page.goto(url);
  await page.waitForFunction(() => document.documentElement.dataset.traceryReady === '1');
  const svg = await page.evaluate(() => tracery.toSVG());
  const state = await page.evaluate(() => tracery.state());
  fs.writeFileSync('mark.svg', svg);
  console.log(state.url);          // permalink: reproduces this mark exactly
  await browser.close();
})();
```

Step by step, if you are driving a browser tool rather than a script:

1. Open `https://pierrelouislabonne.github.io/tracery/?seed=8421&rule=orbit&dark=0&grid=0`
   — `dark=0` gives dark strokes, which is what you want unless the mark is
   going onto a dark surface. See the `dark` trap below.
2. Wait for `document.documentElement.dataset.traceryReady === '1'`.
   The first mark is then drawn and `window.tracery` is callable.
3. Take what you need:
   - `tracery.toSVG()` → SVG string. This is the deliverable: native primitives
     (`circle`, `polygon`, `line`, arc paths), transparent background. Write it
     to a file.
   - `tracery.state()` → `{ seed, rule, ruleInput, dark, grid, fade, url }`.
     Record `url`: it reproduces the mark exactly.

Do not call `tracery.download()` — it triggers a browser download that lands
outside your reach. Use `toSVG()`.

## URL parameters

All optional; each keeps its default when omitted.

| Parameter | Values          | Default |
|-----------|-----------------|---------|
| `seed`    | integer         | random  |
| `rule`    | `auto` or a key | `auto`  |
| `dark`    | `1` / `0`       | `1`     |
| `grid`    | `1` / `0`       | `1`     |
| `fade`    | `1` / `0`       | `1`     |

`grid` is the dotted backdrop — and it is included in the SVG export. Set
`grid=0` before exporting: with `grid=1` the export is ~87 KB instead of ~1 KB.
`fade` makes each stroke fade progressively in opacity along the sequence.

## window.tracery

```js
tracery.generate({ seed, rule, dark, grid, fade })  // re-render, returns state()
tracery.toSVG()                                     // SVG string
tracery.state()                                     // current mark + permalink
tracery.rules()                                     // the 17 rule keys
tracery.geometry()                                  // raw shapes, alphas, dashes
```

All arguments are optional; unspecified options keep their current value.
`generate()` without a seed draws a random one and returns it, so the mark stays
reproducible. Generating in a loop is cheap — no network, no rate limit.

## Composition rules

Pick a key from the intent, or leave `auto` and let the seed decide.

| Key          | Composition                                          | Reads as                     |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| `tangent`    | shrinking shapes sharing one tangency line           | growth, hierarchy            |
| `concentric` | nested copies of one shape around a center           | focus, depth                 |
| `clover`     | 2–5 overlapping circles around a center              | union, community, vesica     |
| `trail`      | one shape repeated along a diagonal                  | motion, speed, extrusion     |
| `rotation`   | a polygon copied at rotated angles                   | energy, symmetry, star       |
| `inscribed`  | circles and polygons alternately inscribed           | structure, nesting           |
| `orbit`      | small satellites spaced on a large circle            | system, network, ecosystem   |
| `stack`      | different shapes resting on one another              | assembly, balance            |
| `arches`     | nested half-shapes on a shared baseline              | arch, shelter, sunset        |
| `grid`       | 2×2 or 3×3 of one shape, often interlocking          | modularity, repetition       |
| `rays`       | a central shape ringed by short radial segments      | sun, radiance, broadcast     |
| `hatching`   | chords filling a shape, or parallel bands            | texture, layers, data        |
| `chevrons`   | stacked Vs, alone or flanking a shape                | direction, progress, signal  |
| `fan`        | segments converging on a point                       | convergence, beam, focus     |
| `horizon`    | a half-shape over receding lines                     | landscape, calm, sun on water|
| `ellipses`   | a circle flattened into narrowing ellipses           | planet, sphere, rotation     |
| `phases`     | one shape repeated along the vertical axis           | cycle, sequence, moon phases |

An unknown key throws from `generate()`; in a URL it is ignored with a console
warning and defaults apply.

## Traps

**Reproduce with `ruleInput`, not `rule`.** `state()` returns both: `rule` is the
rule actually used, `ruleInput` is `auto` when the pick was left to chance. Under
`auto` the seed also drives that pick, so replaying a seed with the *resolved*
rule yields a different mark. The `url` field always carries the right pair.

**`dark=1` draws near-white strokes.** Exports have a transparent background, so
a dark-theme mark placed on a light page is invisible. Use `dark=0` for a mark
that has to stand on its own.

**The grid exports too, and it is huge.** With `grid=1` (the default),
`toSVG()` returns **~87 KB** instead of ~1 KB — the 1521 dots of the backdrop
outweigh the mark by a factor of 88. Set `grid=0` before calling `toSVG()`
unless you genuinely want the dotted background in the file. If you keep it,
write the string straight to disk and never hold it in your context.
